reading.title: Elon Musk — "I wish I had started earlier"
text: Elon Musk was born in 1971 in South Africa. As a boy, he read books all day and taught himself to write computer programs. At 12, he sold his first video game for 500 dollars. He wishes he had kept a copy of it — today it would be a museum piece!

At 17 he moved to Canada with almost no money, and later to the USA. In 1995 he started his first internet company with his brother. They didn't have a flat, so they slept in the office and showered at the gym. Four years later, they sold the company for 300 million dollars.

Musk then created PayPal, an online payment system. When eBay bought it in 2002, he became very rich. Many people wish they could stop working after that. But Musk used almost all of his money to start two new companies: SpaceX (rockets) and Tesla (electric cars). Both nearly went bankrupt in 2008. "I wish I hadn't been so close to losing everything," he said later, "but I would do it again."

Today Tesla is the most valuable car company in the world, and SpaceX rockets fly to the space station. Musk also bought Twitter and renamed it X. Many young people in Uzbekistan wish they could work for him — or become like him. His advice: "If something is important enough, you should do it even if you are afraid."

lessons.title: Infinitive of Purpose
lessons.grammar_topic: MAQSAD INFINITIVI (to + V1 / in order to / so as to / so that)
lessons.test_after: PROGRESS TEST 3 — 14–19-darslar (savollar, conditionals 2–3, during/while, if/unless, indirect questions, wish, infinitive of purpose; crime, travel, food, school, shopping, confusing words)
lessons.book_ref: Student's book IELTS 2.0: Lesson 19 – Infinitive of purpose (jadval); CONFUSING WORDS; Reading — Mirzo Ulug'bek (Jony Academy matni); Audio 51–60.
objectives: Maqsadni to + V1 / in order to / so as to bilan aytish.
so that + gap va for + ot shakllarini farqlash.
Inkor maqsad: in order not to / so as not to.
20 juft chalkash so'zni (accept/except, advice/advise…) farqlab ishlatish; Progress test 3 ga tayyorlanish.
timeline: Ustoz: "Why do you come to Jony Academy?" — "To learn English!" — "Why do you learn English?" — "In order to get 7.0." Doskaga: to + V1 = maqsad.
20 savol, 15 soniya; oldingi dars lug'ati + grammatikasi.

Kitob jadvali: Sentence + to + verb (He went to the gym to work out); Sentence + in order to + verb (She studies hard in order to pass the exam). Qo'shimcha: so as to (rasmiy), so that + S + can/could/will (gap bilan), for + ot (I went out for bread). Inkor: in order not to / so as not to.
Har so'z bilan yangi grammatika qolipida gap.
Kitob: formula → gap → tarjima; warm-up / normativ / coin me'yorlari.
Sinf matni + 3 topshiriq; kitob Topic'lari uyga.
Ko'p uchragan xatolar doskada; STRONG lug'at kuchlilarga.

intro: Maqsad savoli "Why? / What for?" — javob: to + V1: "He went to the gym to work out."
in order to / so as to — rasmiyroq, yozma: "She studies hard in order to pass the exam."
so that + gap: "I saved money so that I could buy a laptop." (ega o'zgarsa yoki modal kerak bo'lsa).
for + ot: "I went to the shop for bread" (for + ot; "for to buy" — xato).
Inkor: "I left early in order not to be late" / "so as not to be late" ("to not be" — og'zaki, yozma emas).
formulas: He went to the gym to work out.
U mashq qilish uchun sport zaliga bordi.
S + V + in order to + V1
She studies hard in order to pass the exam.
U imtihondan o'tish uchun qattiq o'qiydi.
S + V + so as to + V1 (rasmiy)
He left early so as to catch the train.
U poyezdga ulgurish uchun erta chiqdi.
S + V + so that + S + can/could/will
I saved money so that I could buy a laptop.
Noutbuk sotib ola olishim uchun pul yig'dim.
I went to the shop for bread.
in order not to / so as not to + V1
I whispered so as not to wake the baby.
presentation: Why do you learn English?
I learn English to get a good job.
Why did Ulugh Beg build an observatory?
He built it in order to study the stars.

To work out and get fit.

notes: Maqsad = "…uchun" (nima uchun qilyapman). Sabab = "because" (nima uchun bo'ldi). "I study because I want a job" (sabab) vs "I study to get a job" (maqsad).
"for + V-ing" — narsaning vazifasi: "A knife is for cutting" (odam maqsadi emas).
so that + can (hozir/kelajak) / could (o'tgan).
Chalkash so'zlar: talaffuz yoki imlo yaqin, ma'no boshqa: accept (qabul qilmoq) / except (tashqari); advice (ot) / advise (fe'l); quiet (jim) / quite (ancha).
mistakes: I went to the shop for to buy bread.
I went to the shop to buy bread. / for bread.
I study hard for pass the exam.
I study hard to pass the exam.
She left early so that not to be late.
She left early so as not to be late. / so that she wouldn't be late.
I called him for asking a question.
I called him to ask a question.

reading.title: Mirzo Ulugh Beg — the king who counted the stars
text: Mirzo Ulugh Beg was born in 1394. He was the grandson of Amir Temur, and at 15 he became the ruler of Samarkand. But he was not a typical king. He loved mathematics and astronomy more than war. He built madrasas in Samarkand and Bukhara in order to teach science, and he wrote above the door of one of them: "Seeking knowledge is the duty of every Muslim man and woman."

In 1420 he built a huge observatory on a hill near Samarkand. He built it to study the stars and planets. The main instrument was a giant curve, 40 metres long, cut into the rock. Ulugh Beg and his scientists used it to measure the positions of the stars. In order to do this, they worked for years, every clear night.

The result was a catalogue of 1,018 stars — the most accurate in the world for 200 years. Ulugh Beg also measured the length of the year: 365 days, 6 hours, 10 minutes and 8 seconds. Today we know the real number — and he was wrong by less than one minute! Europeans didn't reach this accuracy until the 17th century.

Sadly, in 1449 he was killed, and his observatory was destroyed. For hundreds of years, nobody knew where it was. In 1908, an archaeologist found the underground part of the giant curve. Today you can visit it in Samarkand. There is also a crater on the Moon named after Ulugh Beg — like Al-Khwarizmi and Al-Beruni.

Ulugh Beg's mistake was less than a ___.
Jasur is saving money so that he can study ___ in ___.

kahoot.q: He went to the gym ___ work out.
kahoot.explain: Maqsad (nima uchun?) → to + V1: to work out.

kahoot.q: I went to the shop ___ bread.
kahoot.explain: Keyin OT (bread) keladi → for + ot. Fe'l bo'lsa: to buy bread.

kahoot.q: She studies hard ___ order to pass the exam.
kahoot.explain: Rasmiyroq shakl: in order to + V1.

kahoot.q: I saved money so ___ I could buy a laptop.
kahoot.explain: so that + ega + could/can: so that I could buy...

kahoot.q: I whispered so as ___ wake the baby.
kahoot.explain: Inkor: so as not to / in order not to + V1.

kahoot.q: Qaysi gapda XATO bor?
options: I called him for asking a question.
I called him to ask a question.
I went to the market for some apples.
He left early so as to catch the bus.
kahoot.explain: Odamning maqsadi → to + V1: to ask. «for asking» — xato.

kahoot.q: Tarjima: «U poyezdga ulgurish uchun erta chiqdi.»
options: He left early to catch the train.
He left early for catch the train.
He left early for catching the train.
He left early that catch the train.
kahoot.explain: «...uchun» (maqsad) + fe'l → to + V1: to catch.

kahoot.q: «so that» dan keyin nima keladi?
kahoot.explain: so that + to'liq gap: so that I could buy a laptop.

kahoot.q: I left early in order ___ be late.
kahoot.explain: in order not to + V1 — ...maslik uchun. «to not» — yozmada xato.

kahoot.q: Qaysi gap TO'G'RI?
options: I went to the bank to get some cash.
I went to the bank for get some cash.
I went to the bank for to get some cash.
I went to the bank getting some cash.
kahoot.explain: Maqsad + fe'l → to + V1: to get. «for to» — hech qachon.

kahoot.q: My mum works hard so that we ___ go to a good school.
kahoot.explain: so that + ega (we) + can + V1.

kahoot.q: «Why did you go to the library?» — «___ some books.»
kahoot.explain: Why? savoliga maqsad javobi: To + V1 (To borrow some books).

kahoot.q: Everyone came to the party ___ Ali — he was ill.
kahoot.explain: except — ...dan tashqari. accept — qabul qilmoq, expect — kutmoq.

kahoot.q: Can you ___ me some money until Friday?
kahoot.explain: lend — qarzga BERMOQ (lend me). borrow — qarzga OLMOQ (borrow from).

kahoot.q: My brother is taller ___ me.
kahoot.explain: than — taqqoslash (...dan). then — keyin.

kahoot.q: Can I give you some ___? Don't stay up late before the exam.
kahoot.explain: advice — ot (maslahat), sanalmaydi. advise — fe'l (maslahat bermoq).

kahoot.q: Ice cream is my favourite ___.
kahoot.explain: dessert (ss) — shirinlik. desert (s) — cho'l.

kahoot.q: Smoking can ___ your health.
kahoot.explain: affect — fe'l (ta'sir qilmoq). effect — ot (ta'sir, natija).

kahoot.q: The library is very ___ — nobody is talking.
kahoot.explain: quiet — jim, sokin. quite — ancha, juda.

kahoot.q: These trousers are too ___ — I need a belt.
kahoot.explain: loose — bo'sh, keng. lose — yo'qotmoq.

lessons.title: Modal Verbs: have to, need, must, should
lessons.grammar_topic: MODAL FE'LLAR — HAVE TO / NEED (TO) / MUST / SHOULD
lessons.book_ref: Student's book IELTS 2.0: Lesson 20 – Modal verbs (ikki jadval); HOME AND BUILDINGS; Reading — Amir Temur (Jony Academy matni).
objectives: have to / must / need to / should farqini (majburiyat kuchi va manbai) bilish.
don't have to (shart emas) va mustn't (taqiq) farqini aniq ajratish.
Modal fe'llarni tasdiq, inkor, savolda tuzish; o'tgan zamon: had to.
Uy va binolar CORE 20 bilan uy tasviri va ijara suhbati tuzish.
materials: Home and buildings (uy va binolar) CORE 20 varag'i.
timeline: Ustoz sinf qoidalarini aytadi: "You must switch off your phone. You should do your homework. You don't have to stand up. You needn't shout." — o'quvchilar kuchini baholaydi: qaysi eng qattiq?
Kahoot — Progress test 3 natijalari + infinitive of purpose
20 savol, 15 soniya; oldingi dars lug'ati + grammatikasi.
YOZMA NORMATIV — Progress test 3 natijalari + infinitive of purpose lug'ati

Kitob jadvallari: HAVE TO (tashqi majburiyat; don't have to = shart emas; Do you have to…?), NEED TO / needn't, MUST (ichki/qoidaviy majburiyat; mustn't = taqiq!), SHOULD (maslahat; shouldn't). Doskada shkala: must → have to → need to → should.
Home and buildings (uy va binolar) — CORE 20
Har so'z bilan yangi grammatika qolipida gap.
Kitob: formula → gap → tarjima; warm-up / normativ / coin me'yorlari.
Sinf matni + 3 topshiriq; kitob Topic'lari uyga.
Yangi grammatika bilan 5 gap (yozma) yoki 1 daqiqa og'zaki.
Ko'p uchragan xatolar doskada; STRONG lug'at kuchlilarga.

intro: HAVE TO — tashqi majburiyat (qoida, ish, boshqa odam): "I have to finish this report by tomorrow." O'tgan: had to; kelajak: will have to.
MUST — kuchli majburiyat, ko'pincha o'zim/qonun: "You must follow the safety guidelines." MUSTN'T = TAQIQ: "You mustn't smoke here."
DON'T HAVE TO / NEEDN'T = shart emas (ixtiyoriy): "She doesn't have to do it."
SHOULD — maslahat, to'g'ri ish: "You should apologize for your mistake." shouldn't = qilmagan ma'qul.
formulas: S + have/has to + V1 / don't/doesn't have to / Do/Does + S + have to?
I have to finish this report by tomorrow. / She doesn't have to do it. / Do you have to go there?
Men hisobotni ertagacha tugatishim shart. / U buni qilishi shart emas. / U yerga borishing shartmi?
You must follow the safety guidelines.
S + need to + V1 / needn't + V1
We need to paint the walls. / You needn't come early.
Devorlarni bo'yashimiz kerak. / Erta kelishing shart emas.
S + should/shouldn't + V1 / Should + S + V1?
You should apologize for your mistake. / Should I call the landlord?
Xatong uchun kechirim so'rashing kerak. / Uy egasiga qo'ng'iroq qilaymi?
We had to move last year. / You will have to pay a deposit.
O'tgan yili ko'chishimizga to'g'ri keldi. / Garov puli to'lashingga to'g'ri keladi.
presentation: Do you have to pay rent every month?
Yes, I have to pay it on the first.
Must tenants sign a lease?
Yes, they must sign it before moving in.
Should we paint the living room white?
Yes, you should — it'll look bigger.
Do I have to pay a deposit?
Yes, you have to pay one month's rent.
Can I keep a dog in the flat?
No, you mustn't keep pets here.
Do we need to fix the roof now?
No, you don't have to; it can wait until summer.
What should I do if the lock breaks?
You should call the landlord.
Did you have to move last year?
Yes, we had to move because of my job.
Must I take off my shoes?
Yes, in Uzbek homes you must take off your shoes.
Will we have to renovate the kitchen?
Yes, you'll have to renovate it soon.
notes: must — yozma qoidalar va kuchli shaxsiy fikr; have to — kundalik majburiyat (og'zaki ko'proq).
mustn't ≠ don't have to: mustn't = taqiq, don't have to = ixtiyoriy.
should = maslahat; ought to = should (rasmiy); had better = kuchli maslahat (aks holda muammo).
Uy so'zlari: landlord (uy egasi), tenant (ijarachi), lease (ijara shartnomasi), mortgage (ipoteka).
mistakes: You mustn't come early — it's optional.
You don't have to come early.
Do you have to work? / Must you work?

reading.title: Amir Temur — the ruler who built Samarkand
text: Amir Temur was born in 1336 near Shahrisabz. By 1370 he had become the ruler of Samarkand, and in the next thirty years he created one of the largest empires in history. But today people remember him not only as a general. They remember him as a builder.

Temur believed that a capital city must be beautiful. He brought the best architects, builders and artists from every country he visited — from Iran, India, Syria and Turkey — and they had to work in Samarkand. "If you doubt our power, look at our buildings," he said. Under his rule, the builders built the Bibi-Khanym Mosque, the Shah-i-Zinda complex, and the Ak-Saray palace in Shahrisabz. Its entrance was 40 metres high — visitors had to walk through the biggest door in the world.

Temur's rules were strict. Builders must not stop working, even at night; when Bibi-Khanym was being built, the workers had to use elephants to carry the stones. But he also said that a ruler should protect scientists, poets and craftsmen. He built roads, bridges and caravanserais so that traders could travel safely.

Temur died in 1405 and is buried in the Gur-Emir mausoleum in Samarkand. Its blue dome became the model for many buildings in Central Asia and even in India — the Taj Mahal has the same shape. If you visit Samarkand today, you don't have to be a historian to feel his power: you should simply stand in Registan Square and look up.

kahoot.q: You ___ smoke in the building. It's against the rules.
kahoot.explain: Taqiq (mumkin emas) → mustn't. don't have to / needn't — shart emas.

kahoot.q: I must ___ now — my bus is leaving.
kahoot.explain: must dan keyin to qo'yilmaydi: must + V1 (go).

kahoot.q: Tomorrow is Sunday, so I ___ get up early.
kahoot.explain: Ixtiyoriy, majbur emas → don't have to. mustn't — taqiq bo'lardi.

kahoot.q: She ___ pay the rent on the first day of every month.
kahoot.explain: she → has to + V1. «must to» — xato (to kerak emas).

kahoot.q: You ___ apologise to your neighbour — it's the right thing to do.
kahoot.explain: Maslahat, to'g'ri ish → should + V1.

kahoot.q: Qaysi gapda XATO bor?
options: She has to not pay the deposit.
She doesn't have to pay the deposit.
She has to pay the deposit.
Does she have to pay the deposit?
kahoot.explain: have to inkori do/does bilan: She doesn't have to pay.

kahoot.q: Last year we ___ paint the whole flat ourselves.
kahoot.explain: must ning o'tgan shakli yo'q → had to (Last year — o'tgan).

kahoot.q: Tarjima: «Erta kelishing shart emas.»
kahoot.explain: needn't + V1 = shart emas. mustn't — taqiq (mumkin emas).

kahoot.q: ___ you have to work on Saturdays?
kahoot.explain: have to savoli do/does bilan: Do you have to work...?

kahoot.q: MUSTN'T nimani bildiradi?
kahoot.explain: mustn't = taqiq: You mustn't touch the wires.

kahoot.q: The lift is broken, so we'll ___ use the stairs.
kahoot.explain: will dan keyin must bo'lmaydi → will have to + V1.

kahoot.q: Should I ___ the landlord about the broken window?
kahoot.explain: Should + ega + V1? (to qo'yilmaydi).

kahoot.q: The person who owns the flat and gets the rent is the ___.
kahoot.explain: landlord — uy egasi (ijaraga beruvchi). tenant — ijarachi.

kahoot.q: A person who pays rent to live in a flat is a ___.
kahoot.explain: tenant — ijarachi (ijara haqi to'laydi).

kahoot.q: We keep old boxes in the ___ under the house.
kahoot.explain: basement — yerto'la (pastda). attic — chordoq (tom ostida).

kahoot.q: A very tall building in a big city is a ___.
kahoot.explain: skyscraper — osmono'par bino. cottage — kichik qishloq uyi.

kahoot.q: Before you move in, you pay a ___; you get it back when you leave.
kahoot.explain: deposit — garov puli (qaytariladi). mortgage — ipoteka.

kahoot.q: «ta'mirlash» — inglizcha?
kahoot.explain: renovation — ta'mirlash. foundation — poydevor, inspection — tekshiruv.

kahoot.q: Smoke goes out of the house through the ___.
kahoot.explain: chimney — mo'ri. gutter — tarnov.

kahoot.q: Don't forget to ___ the door when you leave.
kahoot.explain: lock — qulflamoq.

lessons.title: Passive Voice (Simple)
lessons.grammar_topic: MAJHUL NISBAT — PRESENT / PAST / FUTURE SIMPLE PASSIVE (be + V3)
lessons.vocab_topic: Ages and stages of life (yosh va hayot bosqichlari)
lessons.book_ref: Student's book IELTS 2.0: Lesson 21 – Passive voice simple (jadval); AGES AND STAGES; Reading — Alisher Navoiy (Jony Academy matni).
objectives: Active gapni passive'ga o'tkazish: ob'ekt egaga aylanadi, be + V3, bajaruvchi "by" bilan yoki tushiriladi.
Present / Past / Future Simple Passive'ni tasdiq, inkor va savolda tuzish.
Passive qachon kerak: bajaruvchi noma'lum / muhim emas / aniq.
Hayot bosqichlari CORE 20 bilan biografiya aytib berish (was born, was raised, was educated).
materials: Ages and stages of life (yosh va hayot bosqichlari) CORE 20 varag'i.
timeline: Ustoz: "Somebody built this school in 1995." → "This school was built in 1995." Kim qurgani muhim emas — NIMA bo'lgani muhim. Doskaga: be + V3.
20 savol, 15 soniya; oldingi dars lug'ati + grammatikasi.

Kitob jadvali: Present Simple Passive — S + am/is/are + V3 (Schools are built every year); Past Simple Passive — S + was/were + V3 (The hospital was built last year); Future Simple Passive — S + will be + V3 (The hotel will be built next year). "by + bajaruvchi" ixtiyoriy.
Ages and stages of life (yosh va hayot bosqichlari) — CORE 20
Har so'z bilan yangi grammatika qolipida gap.
Kitob: formula → gap → tarjima; warm-up / normativ / coin me'yorlari.
Sinf matni + 3 topshiriq; kitob Topic'lari uyga.
Yangi grammatika bilan 5 gap (yozma) yoki 1 daqiqa og'zaki.
Ko'p uchragan xatolar doskada; STRONG lug'at kuchlilarga.

intro: Active: "People speak English here" → Passive: "English is spoken here". Ob'ekt (English) — yangi ega; fe'l — be + V3.
be zamonni ko'rsatadi: is/are (hozir), was/were (o'tgan), will be (kelajak). V3 o'zgarmaydi.
Bajaruvchi kerak bo'lsa — by: "The poem was written by Navoi." Noma'lum/muhim emas bo'lsa — tushiriladi.
Biografiyada passive ko'p: was born, was raised, was educated, was called, is remembered.
formulas: The hospital was built last year.
The hotel will be built next year.
presentation: Where were you born?
I was born in Fergana.
Where was Navoi born?
He was born in Herat in 1441.
Is Uzbek spoken in Afghanistan?
Yes, it is spoken by millions there.
Who was "Khamsa" written by?
It was written by Navoi.
When was your school built?
It was built in 2005.
Are children raised by grandparents in your family?
Yes, many children are raised by grandparents.
Will the new metro line be opened next year?
Yes, it will be opened in spring.
Was the exam cancelled?
No, it wasn't cancelled.
How are teenagers educated in Uzbekistan?
They are educated at school until 18.
Is plov cooked every Thursday in your family?
Yes, it is cooked every Thursday!
notes: Passive faqat ob'ektli (transitive) fe'llarda: "arrive, happen, sleep" — passive bo'lmaydi.
Ikki ob'ektli fe'llar: "She was given a prize" / "A prize was given to her".
Modal bilan passive: must be done, can be seen, should be finished (20-dars bilan bog'lang).
Yosh bosqichlari: infancy → childhood → adolescence → adulthood → middle age → old age.
mistakes: The book was wrote by Navoi.
The book was written by Navoi.
The bridge was built next year.
The bridge will be built next year.
The letter was sent by yesterday.

reading.title: Alisher Navoi — the poet whose words are still read
text: Alisher Navoi was born in Herat in 1441. He was raised in a family of officials, and his childhood was spent close to the palace. His friend from school was Husayn Bayqara, who later became the ruler of Herat. Navoi was educated in Herat, Mashhad and Samarkand, and by the age of 15 he was already known as a poet.

In the 15th century, most poetry in Central Asia was written in Persian. Turkic — the language of the people — was considered a language of the street, not of literature. Navoi changed this. His poems were written in Old Uzbek (Chagatai), and he proved that this language was as rich as Persian. His most famous work, "Khamsa" (Five Poems), was finished in 1485. More than 26,000 lines were written for it.

Navoi was also a minister. Under him, schools, hospitals, mosques and bridges were built in Herat — more than 300 buildings. Poor students were given money, and artists were supported. He never married and had no children; he said his books were his children.

Navoi died in 1501. Today his name is given to a city, a region, a metro station, a theatre and the national library of Uzbekistan. His poems are still read at weddings and at school, and his words are quoted every day: "If you are a human, you must not be indifferent to people's troubles."

objectives: Present Continuous Passive (hozir bajarilayotgan ish) va Past Continuous Passive (o'tgan paytda bajarilayotgan) ni tuzish.

20 savol, 15 soniya; oldingi dars lug'ati + grammatikasi.
YOZMA NORMATIV — Passive voice simple lug'ati

Kitob jadvali: Present Continuous Passive — S + am/is/are + being + V3 (The hospital is being built); Past Continuous Passive — S + was/were + being + V3 (The hotel was being built); Future Continuous Passive — ishlatilmaydi (N/A). intro: Present Continuous Passive — HOZIR bajarilayotgan ish, bajaruvchi muhim emas: "The hospital is being built" (hozir qurilyapti).
Past Continuous Passive — o'tgan paytda bajarilayotgan edi: "At 5 pm the hotel was being built."
Formula: be (zamonda) + being + V3. "being" o'zgarmaydi.
Future Continuous Passive ishlatilmaydi — o'rniga Future Simple Passive: "will be built".
formulas: The hotel was being built when I came.

reading.title: Lionel Messi — the boy who was paid in hormones
text: Lionel Messi was born in 1987 in Rosario, Argentina. When he was 11, doctors found that he had a growth problem. The treatment cost 1,000 dollars a month, and his family couldn't pay. Clubs in Argentina said no. But in 2000, Barcelona said yes: Messi's treatment was paid by the club, and the first contract was being written on a paper napkin in a café!

Messi moved to Spain at 13. While he was being trained at Barcelona's academy, he was often homesick. But he worked hard. At 17 he played his first match, and soon he was being watched by the whole world. He played for Barcelona for 21 years and scored 672 goals. In 2021 the club had financial problems: too much money was being spent, and Messi had to leave. He cried at his last press conference.

Today Messi plays for Inter Miami in the USA, where he is being paid more than 50 million dollars a year. He has won the World Cup (2022) and the Ballon d'Or eight times — more than any other player. His net worth is being estimated at over one billion dollars.

But Messi is also known for his charity. Millions of dollars are being donated by his foundation to children's hospitals, and sick children are being helped every year. "Money is being given to me because of football," he says, "so it should be given back to people."

lessons.title: Passive Voice (Perfect)
lessons.grammar_topic: MAJHUL NISBAT — PRESENT / PAST / FUTURE PERFECT PASSIVE (have been + V3)
lessons.book_ref: Student's book IELTS 2.0: Lesson 23 – Passive voice perfect (jadval); ON THE ROAD WORDS (50); Reading — Baxodir Jalolov (Jony Academy matni); Audio 71–80.
objectives: Present Perfect Passive (natija hozir), Past Perfect Passive (o'tgan nuqtagacha), Future Perfect Passive (kelajak nuqtagacha) ni tuzish.
Passive oilasini bitta jadvalda ko'rish: is built / is being built / has been built / had been built / will have been built.
"just / already / yet / by" bilan perfect passive.
Yo'l CORE 20 bilan yo'l hodisalari va sayohat haqida gapirish (has been closed, had been repaired).
timeline: Ustoz: "Has the homework been checked? — Yes, it has been checked." Doskaga: has been + V3. "By last Friday it had been checked." "By tomorrow it will have been checked."
20 savol, 15 soniya; oldingi dars lug'ati + grammatikasi.
YOZMA NORMATIV — Passive voice continuous lug'ati

Kitob jadvali: Present Perfect Passive — S + have/has + been + V3 (Schools have been built); Past Perfect Passive — S + had + been + V3 (The hospital had been built by 2020); Future Perfect Passive — S + will have + been + V3 (The hotel will have been built by 2050). Uch passive oilasi jadvali: simple / continuous / perfect.
Har so'z bilan yangi grammatika qolipida gap.
Kitob: formula → gap → tarjima; warm-up / normativ / coin me'yorlari.
Sinf matni + 3 topshiriq; kitob Topic'lari uyga.
Ko'p uchragan xatolar doskada; STRONG lug'at kuchlilarga.

intro: Present Perfect Passive — ish bajarilgan, natija hozir: "The road has been closed" (yo'l yopilgan — hozir yopiq).
Past Perfect Passive — o'tgan nuqtagacha bajarilgan edi: "By 2020 the bridge had been built."
Future Perfect Passive — kelajak nuqtagacha bajarilgan bo'ladi: "By 2050 the hotel will have been built."
Formula: have/has/had/will have + been + V3. "been" o'zgarmaydi.
formulas: The hospital had been built by 2020.
The hotel will have been built by 2050.
The road hasn't been repaired yet.
is built / is being built / has been built
The bridge is built. / is being built. / has been built.
presentation: Has the road been repaired yet?
Yes, it has just been repaired.
Had the bridge been built before you moved here?
Yes, it had been built by 2015.
Will the motorway have been finished by next year?
Yes, it will have been finished by summer.
Has your car ever been stolen?
No, it has never been stolen.
Have the road signs been changed?
Yes, new signs have been put up.
Had the tyre been checked before the trip?
No, it hadn't been checked — that's why it went flat.
Has the driver been fined?
Yes, he has been fined for speeding.
Has Jalolov been beaten in his professional career?
No, he has never been beaten.
Will all the tickets have been sold by Friday?
Yes, they will have been sold by then.
Had the accident been reported when the police came?
Yes, it had already been reported.
notes: already / just / yet / ever / never — have va been orasida: "has already been done", "has never been beaten".
by + vaqt → Past Perfect / Future Perfect Passive.
Modal + perfect passive: "should have been checked" (tekshirilishi kerak edi).
Yo'l so'zlari: traffic jam (tirbandlik), rush hour (tig'iz vaqt), breakdown (buzilish), detour (aylanma yo'l).
mistakes: The bridge had been built by 2020.

reading.title: Bakhodir Jalolov — the Big Uzbek who has never been beaten
text: Bakhodir Jalolov was born in 1994 in Sariosiyo, a small town in the Surkhandarya region. He is two metres tall, and his nickname is "Big Uzbek". Boxing has been loved in his family for generations: he was taken to the boxing gym by his father when he was a small boy, and his first fight was won at the age of 12.

By 2016, Jalolov had been chosen for the Uzbek Olympic team. In Tokyo (2021) he was given the gold medal in the super-heavyweight division, and in Paris (2024) he did it again. He has been called the best amateur boxer of his generation, and he has been given the title of "Hero of Uzbekistan".

Jalolov also fights as a professional. Since 2018, more than 14 professional fights have been won by him, and he has never been beaten. Most of his opponents have been knocked out in the first rounds. Boxing experts say that by 2030 he will have been recognised as a world heavyweight champion.

Outside the ring, he is quiet and modest. A sports school has been built in Sariosiyo with his help, and hundreds of boys have been trained there. "Everything I have has been given to me by my parents and my country," he says. "Now it must be given back."

objectives: -ed (his) va -ing (sabab/xususiyat) sifatlarini farqlash va to'g'ri tanlash.
15 ta juftni bilish va gapda ishlatish (bored/boring, excited/exciting, tired/tiring…).
Predloglar: interested IN, excited ABOUT, bored WITH, surprised AT/BY, tired OF.
Transport CORE 20 bilan qatnov va sayohat haqida gapirish (an exciting flight, a tiring journey).
timeline: Ustoz zerikkan yuz bilan: "I am bored." Keyin darsga ishora qilib: "This lesson is boring?!" — sinf kuladi. Farq: -ed = mening hissim; -ing = narsaning xususiyati.
20 savol, 15 soniya; oldingi dars lug'ati + grammatikasi.
YOZMA NORMATIV — Passive voice perfect lug'ati

Kitob jadvali: -ed sifatlar — his-tuyg'uni tasvirlaydi (I am bored by this movie); -ing sifatlar — odam, narsa yoki vaziyatning xususiyatini tasvirlaydi (The movie is boring). Juftlar ro'yxati: bored/boring, interested/interesting, excited/exciting, tired/tiring, surprised/surprising…
Har so'z bilan yangi grammatika qolipida gap.
Kitob: formula → gap → tarjima; warm-up / normativ / coin me'yorlari.
Sinf matni + 3 topshiriq; kitob Topic'lari uyga.
Ko'p uchragan xatolar doskada; STRONG lug'at kuchlilarga.

intro: -ED — odam NIMA HIS QILADI: I'm bored, tired, excited, interested, surprised.
-ING — narsa/odam QANDAY (his uyg'otadi): The film is boring, the trip is tiring, the news is exciting.
Ikkalasi odam haqida bo'lishi mumkin: "He is bored" (zerikkan) vs "He is boring" (zeriktiradigan odam!).
Predloglar: interested in, excited about, bored with, tired of, surprised at/by, worried about, frightened of.
formulas: I am bored by this film.
He is bored. / He is boring.
He is bored (zerikkan) / He is boring (zeriktiradigan).

I'm interested in trains. / I'm tired of traffic.

Ko'p uchraydigan juftlar: amazed/amazing, annoyed/annoying, confused/confusing, disappointed/disappointing, embarrassed/embarrassing, exhausted/exhausting, frightened/frightening, relaxed/relaxing, shocked/shocking, worried/worrying.

reading.title: Diyora Keldiyorova — an amazing Olympic champion
text: Diyora Keldiyorova was born in 1998 in Tashkent. When she was a child, she was interested in many sports, but judo was the most exciting for her. Her parents were worried at first — judo is a hard sport for a girl, they thought. But her coach was impressed by her speed, and Diyora was determined.

Her training is exhausting: six hours a day, six days a week. For years, the results were disappointing — she lost in the early rounds of big competitions. But she was never discouraged. In 2021 she was surprised to win a medal at the World Championships, and after that everything changed.

The Paris Olympics in 2024 were the most thrilling days of her life. In the final she beat the Olympic champion from Kosovo in just a few minutes. It was an astonishing result: Diyora became the first Uzbek woman to win an Olympic gold medal in any sport. Millions of Uzbeks were amazed and proud; the streets of Tashkent were full of excited fans at 2 am.

"I was tired, but I was so relieved and happy," she said afterwards. Today she is an inspiring example for thousands of girls in Uzbekistan, and judo clubs are crowded with new students. Her next goal? "The 2028 Olympics — it will be even more exciting."

IELTS 2.0 kursi bo'yicha grammatika xaritasi va eng muhim 60 so'zni takrorlash; final testga tayyorlanish.
materials: Revision — IELTS 2.0 eng muhim 60 so'z CORE 20 varag'i.
timeline: Ustoz: "I taught myself to cook. Who taught you English? — Jony Academy! Did you teach yourself anything?" — har o'quvchi "I taught myself to …" gapi.
20 savol, 15 soniya; oldingi dars lug'ati + grammatikasi.

Kitob jadvali: myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves — ega va ob'ekt bir xil bo'lganda (She cut herself); urg'u (We built it ourselves); by myself = yolg'iz; each other (bir-birini) bilan farq. Keyin doskada 25 darsning grammatika xaritasi.
Revision — IELTS 2.0 eng muhim 60 so'z — CORE 20
Har so'z bilan yangi grammatika qolipida gap.
Kitob: formula → gap → tarjima; warm-up / normativ / coin me'yorlari.
Sinf matni + 3 topshiriq; kitob Topic'lari uyga.
Ko'p uchragan xatolar doskada; STRONG lug'at kuchlilarga.

intro: O'zlik olmoshi — ish egaga qaytganda: "She cut herself while cooking" (o'zini kesib oldi).
Urg'u: "We built the bookshelf ourselves" (boshqa hech kim emas, o'zimiz).
by + o'zlik olmoshi = yolg'iz, yordamsiz: "He lives by himself."
each other — bir-birini: "They help each other" (u — unga, u — unga); "They help themselves" — har biri o'ziga.
Iboralar: enjoy yourself (maza qil), help yourself (o'zing ol), behave yourself (o'zingni tut), make yourself at home.
formulas: I bought myself a new book. / You can help yourself to some snacks.
O'zimga yangi kitob oldim. / O'zingiz gazak oling.
he … himself / she … herself / it … itself
He taught himself to play the guitar. / She cut herself while cooking.
U gitara chalishni o'zi o'rgandi. / U ovqat pishirayotib o'zini kesib oldi.
we … ourselves / you (pl) … yourselves / they … themselves
We built the bookshelf ourselves. / Please make yourselves at home.
Javonni o'zimiz yasadik. / O'zingizni uydagidek his qiling.
The president himself opened the school.
Beruni worked by himself for years.
Ibn Sina and Beruni wrote to each other.
Ibn Sino va Beruniy bir-biriga xat yozishgan.
presentation: Did you teach yourself English?
No, I learned it at Jony Academy — but I taught myself the alphabet.
Did she hurt herself?
Yes, she cut herself while cooking.
Do you live by yourself?
No, I live with my family.
Did they build the house themselves?
Yes, they built it themselves.
Did you enjoy yourselves at the party?
Yes, we enjoyed ourselves a lot.
Do you and your sister help each other?
Yes, we help each other with homework.
Did the teacher herself check the tests?
Yes, she checked them herself.
Can I take a cake?
Of course — help yourself!
Did Beruni measure the Earth by himself?
Yes, he did the calculations himself.
What have you learned about yourself this course?
I've learned that I can speak English!
notes: Ko'plik: yourselves (siz — ko'p), themselves, ourselves; "theirselves / hisself" — xato.
Ba'zi fe'llardan keyin self yo'q: relax, concentrate, feel, wash/shave/dress (odatda): "I feel good" (myself emas).
Final test tarkibi: 25 formula (har darsdan 1), 50 so'z (har darsdan CORE 2), 10 tarjima, reading (matn + 5 savol), writing (100 so'z: "My plans by 2030").
Grammatika xaritasi: Perfect oilasi (1–6, 9–13) → taqqoslash (7–8) → bog'lovchilar (11, 16) → shart (15) → savol/wish/infinitive (14, 17–19) → modal/passive (20–23) → sifat/olmosh (24–25).
mistakes: We looked at ourselves and smiled. (bir-biriga)
We looked at each other and smiled.

how: CORE 20 — 1–8-darslardan eng muhim so'zlar; STRONG — 9–16; SUPER — 17–24. Har so'zga o'z darsining grammatikasi bilan gap.
Final test oldidan: har o'quvchi 60 so'zdan 10 tasini "o'zi" tanlab, gap tuzadi (I chose these words myself).

reading.title: Abu Rayhan Beruni — the man who measured the Earth himself
text: Abu Rayhan Beruni was born in 973 in Kath, the old capital of Khorezm. He didn't come from a rich family, and he often said that he had taught himself most of what he knew. By the age of 17 he had already measured the position of the Sun, and by 22 he had written his first book about maps.

Beruni was a polymath: he studied astronomy, mathematics, geography, history, medicine and languages. He knew Khorezmian, Persian, Arabic, Sanskrit and Greek. He and Ibn Sina wrote letters to each other and argued about science — the two greatest minds of Central Asia, discussing physics by post!

In 1017 Beruni was taken to Ghazni (today's Afghanistan) by Sultan Mahmud, and from there he travelled to India many times. He learned Sanskrit by himself and wrote "India", the first scientific book about Indian culture, religion and science. Indians themselves say that nobody described their country better than this Uzbek scholar.

His most astonishing achievement was made in India. Standing on a mountain, Beruni measured the radius of the Earth himself with a simple instrument. His result was 6,339 km — the real number is 6,371 km. The difference is less than 1 percent! Europeans reached this accuracy only 600 years later.

Beruni wrote more than 150 books and died in 1048. Today a university, a district and a crater on the Moon are named after him. He believed that knowledge belongs to everybody: "I don't do this for money or a king," he wrote, "I do it for myself and for those who come after me."

items: More than ___ words have been learned.

kahoot.q: I taught ___ to swim.
kahoot.explain: Ega va ob'ekt bir odam → myself.

kahoot.q: They helped ___ to the snacks.
kahoot.explain: they → themselves. «theirselves» degan so'z yo'q.

kahoot.q: She cut ___ while she was cooking.
kahoot.explain: she → herself (o'zini kesib oldi).

kahoot.q: My grandfather lives by ___.
kahoot.explain: by + o'zlik olmoshi = yolg'iz: by himself.

kahoot.q: Qaysi gapda XATO bor?
options: We enjoyed ourselves at the party.
kahoot.explain: feel dan keyin o'zlik olmoshi kerak emas: I feel tired.

kahoot.q: Ibn Sina and Beruni wrote letters to ___.
kahoot.explain: Biri ikkinchisiga → each other. themselves — har biri o'ziga.

kahoot.q: «Can I take a cake?» — «Of course, help ___!»
kahoot.explain: help yourself — o'zingiz oling (mehmonga).

kahoot.q: I ___ Samarkand last summer.
kahoot.explain: «last summer» — aniq o'tgan vaqt → Past Simple (visited).

kahoot.q: This school ___ in 2015.
kahoot.explain: Maktab o'zi qurmaydi → passive, 2015 → was built.

kahoot.q: If I ___ rich, I would buy a house for my parents.
kahoot.explain: Type 2: If + Past Simple (were), would + V1.

kahoot.q: The metro is ___ than the bus.
kahoot.explain: Qisqa sifat: fast → faster than. «more faster» — xato.

kahoot.q: Do you know where ___?
kahoot.explain: Bilvosita savol: ega + fe'l (the station is).

kahoot.q: You ___ park here — it's not allowed.
kahoot.explain: Ruxsat yo'q (taqiq) → mustn't.

kahoot.q: My grandfather ___ away last year. We miss him a lot.
kahoot.explain: pass away — olamdan o'tmoq.

kahoot.q: I'm so ___ — the exam is over and I passed!
kahoot.explain: relieved — yengil tortgan. anxious — xavotirda.

kahoot.q: Ali always does his work on time. He is very ___.
kahoot.explain: reliable — ishonchli.

kahoot.q: The doctor gave me a ___ for some medicine.
kahoot.explain: prescription — dori retsepti.

kahoot.q: «hozirgacha» — inglizcha?
kahoot.explain: so far — hozirgacha. as soon as — ...bilanoq.

kahoot.q: A long time with no rain is a ___.
kahoot.explain: drought — qurg'oqchilik. forecast — ob-havo ma'lumoti.

kahoot.q: Our parents' wedding ___ is on 5 May — 25 years together!
kahoot.explain: anniversary — yillik (to'y yilligi).
